evidence.description: public nonisolated(unsafe) static let shared = EcosiaAuthUIStateProvider(accountsProvider: accountsProviderFactory())

candidates.explanation: The 'shared' singleton instance is declared as 'nonisolated(unsafe)', which bypasses Swift's concurrency safety checks. Since the class manages published properties and interacts with shared services, this could lead to data races if accessed from multiple threads.
candidates.title: Potential Thread Safety Issue with Shared Singleton

candidates.explanation: The method 'handleUserProfileUpdate' is marked with @MainActor, but it internally creates a new Task with @MainActor to update 'isLoggedIn'. This is redundant as the method is already guaranteed to run on the main actor.
candidates.title: Redundant Task Creation on Main Actor

evidence.description: The class maintains three private variables for NSObjectProtocol observers and manually removes them in deinit.

candidates.explanation: The class manually manages NSObjectProtocol observers and removes them in deinit. In modern Swift, using the closure-based API with a storage mechanism or a dedicated wrapper is preferred to avoid potential leaks or missed removals if deinit is not reached as expected.
candidates.title: Manual NotificationCenter Observer Management

candidates.explanation: The 'animateBalanceChange' method uses hardcoded 'asyncAfter' delays (1.0 and 3.0 seconds). This makes the UI behavior rigid and difficult to adjust or test without modifying the source code.
candidates.title: Hardcoded Animation Delays
